No, that is not correct.

In Switzerland, the **franchise (franchise)** is a mandatory **annual deductible** that you must pay out of pocket before your insurance coverage kicks in. The **standard minimum franchise** is **CHF 300 per year**, not CHF 150.

There is also a **maximum limit on the co‑payments (or “patient share”)** after the franchise is met. Once you have paid the full franchise amount in a calendar year, your insurer covers its share of the costs, and you only pay a **maximum of 10 % of the costs (up to a maximum of CHF 700 per year)** for co‑payments. After you reach this CHF 700 cap, the insurance pays 100 % of the remaining costs for the rest of that year.

So the correct points are:

* **Franchise:** Minimum CHF 300 per year (you can choose to pay a higher franchise, up to CHF 2,500, which reduces your monthly premium).
* **Co‑payments after franchise:** Limited to **10 % of the cost (max CHF 700 per year)**.

If you have any further questions about health insurance in Switzerland, feel free to ask.
